title: I made a crime game with Codex. The demo is out—does it actually look fun?
author: freesoulapps
selftext:
I’ve been working on FIXER, a top-down crime game with driving, shooting and jobs around the city. 

There’s a free Windows demo with three missions now.

Started in Three.js, then moved to Unity. Used Codex heavily, and spent a lot of time finding things that were supposedly “fixed” but clearly weren’t when I played. 

Sending screenshots of specific problems worked better than asking it to polish the game.

I’m too close to it now to judge the first impression. Would you try this? And if you do, tell me where you got bored or confused. That’s what I need to hear.

https://alexv2007gmailcom.itch.io/fixer-demo⁠

Windows, \~739 MB. Extract the ZIP and run FIXER-Demo.exe. AI use is disclosed on the page.

comments.author: Savings_Cloud5486
comments.body: nice, why you moved from threejs ?

replies.author: freesoulapps
replies.body:
Mostly performance. As FIXER got heavier, the Three.js build was averaging ~25 FPS on my GTX 1080 / i5-4590 test box. After migrating the same game to Unity it was ~59 FPS on the same hardware.
Unity also gives me a better base for scaling the project, but performance was the main reason I moved.

comments.author: connected_user93
comments.body: Your title card is literally just a random white font on a blue background with some faint lines. It needs a lot of help in the art / art style department otherwise it will remain looking soulless and amateur,

replies.author: freesoulapps
replies.body: Fair criticism. The title card and some of the UI presentation are definitely weaker than the gameplay right now and still read too much like placeholder art. I focused on getting the demo playable first, but the visual identity needs a proper art-direction pass. Thanks for calling it out.

comments.author: HobbyistMoon
comments.body: It reminds me of early gtas

replies.author: freesoulapps
replies.body: Yeah 😄 The idea actually started after I was talking with a friend about how much I enjoyed GTA 2 back in the day. That conversation made me want to try building something with that old-school top-down crime-game feel.
